page.title: AI
page.description: Choose which AI provider FixFlow's assistant uses. AI is off until you pick one.
page.denied: Access Denied. Only administrators can manage AI settings.
page.load_failed: The AI settings could not be loaded.

status.off_text: Nothing is sent to any AI provider. Pick one below to turn it on.
status.environment: This comes from the server's .env file (AI_ENABLED and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). Saving a choice here replaces it.
status.incomplete: A provider is chosen but its settings are not complete, so AI stays off.

help.none: No AI. The assistant is hidden.
help.anthropic: Claude, on Anthropic's service. Needs a key from Anthropic.
help.openai_compatible: OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq or any service on the internet that speaks the OpenAI chat API.
help.local: A model you run yourself (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp). It must be on this server or your own network, so no data leaves.

field.model_local_help: The name of the model the program serves, for example llama3.1.
field.base_url_openai_compatible: The service's address, ending in /v1. It must start with https://. For example https://api.openai.com/v1.
field.base_url_local: Where the program listens. Ollama: http://localhost:11434/v1. If FixFlow runs in Docker and the model runs on the same machine, use http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1.
field.api_key_saved: Saved. Leave blank to keep it.
field.api_key_note: Kept encrypted and never shown again. It is sent only to {{where}}.
field.api_key_host: If you change the address to another host, enter the key again: a key belongs to the host it was given for.
field.api_key_environment: The key is set in the server's .env file. Enter it here to move it into FixFlow.

privacy.title: Where your data goes
privacy.anthropic: Work order details are sent to Anthropic's service (api.anthropic.com) when someone uses the assistant. Read Anthropic's terms to see how it handles them.
privacy.openai_compatible: Work order details are sent over the internet to the service at {{where}} when someone uses the assistant. Read that service's terms to see how it handles them.
privacy.local: Work order details are sent only to {{where}}, which FixFlow has checked is on this server or a private network. FixFlow cannot see what that machine does with them.
privacy.sent: Asset names, work order titles and descriptions, checklists, past work notes, text from attached manuals, and counts of what is open on an asset (work orders, sensor alerts, unusual readings)

actions.test_note: Asks the model one fixed question. No work order data is sent.
actions.save_failed: The settings could not be saved.
actions.remove_confirm: Forget the AI settings? FixFlow will stop using the provider and forget every saved key.

features.title: What it powers
features.assist: FixFlow Assist: a chat on each work order that answers from the asset's history and manuals
features.needs_ai: Choose a provider above to use these.

label.priority: Suggest a priority for new work orders
label.limits: Warn when a sensor is heading for its limit
label.parts: Forecast parts that may run short

help.priority: Adds a button to the new work order form that suggests a priority and says why. The person decides. It sends the title, the description and what is open on the asset to {{where}}.
help.anomalies: Flags a reading far outside what that sensor usually reads, learned from the sensor's own last two weeks, with no limits to set. It is worked out on this server: nothing is sent to the provider.
help.limits: For a sensor that has been steadily rising or falling towards a limit set on an alert rule, says about when it will get there, with a range. Worked out on this server from the last 30 days: nothing is sent to the provider.
help.parts: Says which parts may not last the next 30 days, from how much was used in the last months and what is in stock and on order. Worked out on this server: nothing is sent to the provider.

priority.same: That is the priority you chose.
priority.failed: A priority could not be suggested.

note.anthropic: The title, description and asset details are sent to Anthropic. You choose the priority.
note.openai_compatible: The title, description and asset details are sent to your AI service. You choose the priority.
note.local: The title, description and asset details are sent to your own model. You choose the priority.

anomalies.title: Unusual readings
anomalies.intro: Readings far outside what that sensor usually reads, found from its own last two weeks. No limits were set.
anomalies.action_failed: Could not update it. Try again.

limits.title: Heading for a limit
limits.intro: Sensors on course to reach a limit set on an alert rule, from how they moved over the last 30 days. A forecast, not a promise: it only says something when the movement is clear.
limits.none: No sensor is clearly heading for a limit.
limits.rising: {{metric}} is {{current}} and rising by {{rate}} a day
limits.falling: {{metric}} is {{current}} and falling by {{rate}} a day
limits.basis: from {{history}} days of readings ({{points}} days used), rule: {{rule}}
limits.range_narrow: A narrow range: the readings follow the line closely

parts.title: Parts that may run short
parts.intro: What is expected to be used over the next 30 days, from the last months of use, against what is in stock and on order. A forecast, not a promise. Work that is planned but not yet logged is not in it.
parts.none: No part is expected to run short.
parts.expected: Expected use over the next 30 days: {{expected}} {{unit}} (likely {{low}} to {{high}})
parts.basis: from {{periods}} months of use, logged {{uses}} times
